rubric_notes: Complete. Verified release, a.22 single superfamily, homology endpoint, five families with sunids and members, duplication annotation, linker histone a.4.5.13 and H-NS a.155 lineages via parent calls. Distinguishes family vs superfamily strength, rejects function/template transfer to TAF/NF-Y/SOS, and explicitly says absence of a positive homology claim is not proof of convergence. Notes search bound and automated-match caveat. HDAC/Dot1 placements correct though search not in bundle. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Verified lineages and annotations match bundle. Superfamily-level remote homology stated with explicit note that different families do not imply non-homology (addresses must_avoid directly). Function-transfer limits for PR-ATP, (d)NTP, metal, oligomeric state, template use all stated; Li/UNL correctly dismissed as crystallization content. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1; 2026-10-14.

Correct families with sunids under c.55.1, fold/class lineage, duplication comment and homology record, all evidence-supported. Infers divergent homology from a duplicated ancestral nucleotide-binding domain, with shared ATP cleft and possible hinge mechanism framed as a hypothesis. Refuses to transfer function, substrate, reaction or cellular role (polymerization/chaperone examples cover oligomeric state); regulation is not named explicitly but the principle is clearly stated. Fold-level caveat correct. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Hierarchy, sunids, fold and superfamily comments, family members, Pfam PF05067 and release/periodic-update facts all supported by bundle. Correct superfamily-vs-fold reasoning, notes SCOPe neither asserts homology nor convergence for other a.25 superfamilies, rejects cross-family transfer, names structural alignment, biochemical and profile evidence needed. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1; 2026-10-14.

Evaluator claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-14. Leads with the correct conclusion (probable homology, no function transfer). Hierarchy, family sunids, comments, Pfam xrefs and homology endpoint all verified against bundle. Clearly separates superfamily-level ancestry from family-level function, notes the hedged 'probably related' wording, rejects transfer in both directions, limits template use to fold level, and lists the independent evidence a metal-binding claim would need. States what was not checked. Complete.

Evaluator claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-14. All classifications, sunids, sibling families and d.15 sibling superfamilies match the bundle. Superfamily relationship correctly characterised as probable distant common origin, stronger than fold but weaker than family; explicitly states that a different superfamily is not proof of non-homology. Rejects transfer of conjugation, p97 cofactor binding and Ras binding by name, plus within-family partner specificity and template interchangeability; lists required external evidence and states what was not checked. Complete.

Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14. Families, sunids, fold comment, annotations and homology-endpoint scopes (sf for c.23.1, fa for each family) all supported by bundle. Correctly identifies superfamily as the lowest shared, homology-bearing level, distinguishes remote from close homology, rejects phosphorylation/two-component, catalytic and reverse transfers, notes Pfam mapping is automatic, template limits, and that different superfamilies do not prove convergence. Multidomain context of ODC and KaiA addressed with background-knowledge caveat.

Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14. All must_include met: b.84.5 within fold b.84 with correct sunids (310577, 51229, 310616, 310706, 310707) and species, all supported by bundle; fold-level = architecture only, separate superfamily = no asserted ancestry with b.84.1-b.84.4, and explicitly not a claim of non-homology; family b.84.5.1 groups homologous V1/A1 bulge domains. Background knowledge (NHR absent from F1 beta) clearly flagged as unverified. Function/template transfer limits stated. No material errors.

All classifications, sunids, curator comments, Pfam mapping, and homology records supported by bundle. Correctly states homology is asserted only within superfamilies, rejects both merging and the unrelated/convergent inference, uses the f.21.3 possible-link comment appropriately, limits transfer, and names sequence/profile, inspected ligand alignments, and published structural analysis as needed evidence. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Verified sunids, superfamily/fold/class, fold annotation, family comment, PF02254 and sibling families, all matching the bundle. Superfamily = probable common ancestry despite low sequence similarity; separate families = no close relationship with divergent settings (ADH coenzyme domain with catalytic partner, CoA binding, regulatory RCK/KTN). Bars transfer of function, ligand, mechanism and templates; fold-level similarity to c.3/c.4 not homology; representative caveat; states that cofactor specificity and motifs need separate experimental evidence. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Correct lineage (class k 58788 > k.40 100903 > k.40.1 100904 > k.40.1.1 100905; proteins 103785/100906, species 103786/64668), all supported by bundle. Cites the family 100905 'not a true family' comment and explains that the generic homology_implied_by_level=true default does not override it. Calibrated: designed structural grouping, homology concept does not apply, no function/ligand transfer, explicitly declines a convergence claim. Phrase 'neither has a common ancestor' is slightly strong but immediately qualified.

All must_include met and bundle-supported: 1.69 d1t1ja_/d1t1jb_ c.137.1.1 own fold vs d1f8ya_ c.23.14.1 (shared only class); 2.08 d1t1ja1/d1t1jb1 (1-118) c.23.14.2 vs d1f8ya_ c.23.14.1 under renamed superfamily 52309; sunid continuity; tag domains split as l.1.1.1. Interprets the change as upward to superfamily level implying probable common ancestry, explicitly not a family merge, matching the paper's remote-relationship example. Limits on function/template transfer; honest that intermediates were not checked. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

All criteria met with bundle-supported identifiers, both domains' annotations (Fab NC10 comment, complexed with ca/man/nag) and the homology warning. Clear statement that l.1.1.1 sharing says nothing about ancestry, that 8 residues cannot support even fold-level similarity, and that function cannot be transferred from family placement. Notes sequence endpoint 404 honestly. Evaluator: claude-fable-5-1; 2026-10-14.

Correct whole-chain 1.75 assignment (d1acca_, 43828, f.11.1.1), unchanged in 2.01 and 2.03, split from 2.04 and identical through 2.08 with both sids, sunids, boundaries and lineages; transparently notes that 2.02 was not queried without weakening the conclusion. Reads the split as recognition of a reusable PA14-like module shared with adhesin and glycoside-hydrolase families, states that the two halves' lowest common level is the root so no homology is claimed yet unrelatedness is not proven, and cautions that the single C-terminal domain does not mirror the literature's structural subregions. Search guidance is per-domain, region-wise and release-pinned, with unverified items listed.

All must_include met with bundle-verified sids, boundaries, sccs and sunids (fold 345891/sf 345924/fa 345979; family 159638 predating 3jb9 with yeast and human species nodes). Distinguishes superfamily-level homology from Prp8-specific families, states new fold d.394 makes no homology claim and does not prove independent origin, rejects function transfer, labels group II intron hypothesis as background knowledge. No must_avoid violations. Minor overreach stating no warnings for all five domains when bundle covers a1 annotations and a5 homology only; not material. Evaluator: claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-14.

Complete: frames a.298.1.1 as a repeat family whose classified unit is the superhelical array, cites the 're' flag and its definition, the canonical repeat 4cj9 A:259-292 in d4cj9a_, the representative-only coordinate scope, and the family homology record (implied at family level, no warnings). Correctly states family placement exceeds fold/class evidence and that BurrH is grouped at family level despite divergent repeats. Limits cover repeat counting, RVD-based specificity non-transfer, the one-repeat NMR fragment as a bad template, and no quality-based ranking. Evaluator: Claude SCOPe benchmark grader, 2026-10-14.

Correct, supported metadata (2.08, 2.08-stable, dates, periodic 2.08-2026-08-16). Cites stable 2.08 pinned in paths, rejects 'current', and preserves the dated label alongside (not instead of) 2.08. Correctly says periodic update is not a new stable and does not replace 2.08. However, it never states what periodic updates contain (newly classified PDB entries added without rewriting stable domains), only that the endpoint does not say, so must_include item 3 is only partially met.

All required content present and bundle-supported: same a.47.2.1 lineage; fragment comment plus 'ms' heterogeneity flag in 2.08 (absent in 1.75, 'mutant' on 1br0); d1dn1b_ now automated match to curated d3c98b_ after 1dn1 obsolescence; fold defined by four long helices so the three-helix fragments' STAT-like label is inherited from the complete domain. Correctly notes SCOPe makes no spectrin homology or non-homology claim, keeps homology at family/superfamily, bars function/partner/conformation transfer, recommends full-domain templates with caveats, and states what was not retrieved. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Correctly uses the c.2 homology record ('levels above superfamily do not imply homology') and c.2 binding-mode comment; divergence confined to superfamily, convergence 'very likely' across folds and two classes (c.2 vs d.166.1), with explicit limits that separate superfamilies are not proof of unrelatedness and c.2/c.3/c.4 remain unresolved. Evidence needed to call a pair analogous or homologous is spelled out (topology, binding orientation, HMM coverage/E-values, FATCAT/DALI full-length significance). All sunids (51735, 51734, 51905, 52467, 56399, 55347), fold cores and class placements supported by bundle. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Complete on both release states: 2.04 different folds and superfamilies with lineages and sunids, 2.05 already b.18.1.36, 2.08 shared superfamily with families b.18.1.36 and b.18.1.3 separate, and correct treatment of the two-residue l.1.1.1 segment. Cites the retrieved family comment and the 2.08 placements of d2quoa_ and d1w99a3, and labels the structure-comparison figures as representative evidence for 1nqjA rather than 1nqdA. Unusually careful on inference limits: states the structural hits alone do not discriminate homology from shared fold, points out comparable scores from other folds and superfamilies consistent with the old CUB-like placement, notes Cry3A's own domain was absent from the retrieved page, and declines to transfer ligand, receptor, specificity or mechanism in either direction. Some named lower-ranked hits fall beyond the truncated portion of the bundle and were not penalized. Evaluator: Claude, 2026-10-14.

Lineage, sunids, boundaries, comments, hf definition, homology flags and quality values all match the evidence, and quality is correctly framed as representativeness rather than homology. Reasoning complete on homology retention, fold mismatch, template/training/function transfer, leakage and hf stratification. One unsupported factual error: states d1p7jd_ is DNA-bound in 1p7j and refers to 'the 1p7j complex'; the retrieved comment is 'complexed with nhe; mutant' and 1p7j is the free K52E mutant, not a DNA complex.

Reasoning complete: family homology unchanged by fr flag; SEQRES 99 vs ATOM 50 with alignment coverage caveats; prefer complete unflagged d1uc6a1 or another full tissue-factor domain, fragment left out or kept only with flag preserved; fragment counts for membership but not structural variation; no function/ligand transfer. Identifiers and annotations correct. Explicitly did not retrieve SPACI/AEROSPACI/resolution, so cannot rank on quality and representative choice rests on completeness alone. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Evaluator claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-14. All must_include met: new superfamily in existing fold with one new family; family in existing superfamily = remote-homology claim requiring integrated evidence; new fold needs different core topology, not peripheral insertions; placement is provisional and revisable; explicitly states different superfamilies mean no homology assertion, not evidence of absence. Rejects fold-level function/template transfer. b.1 example (sunid 48725, 33 superfamilies b.1.1-b.1.33, named members) fully supported by the bundle (has_more false, last child b.1.33).

All classifications, sunids, fold/superfamily annotations and the sf-scope homology record are correct and bundle-supported. Distinguishes general-knowledge mechanism from SCOPe records, treats ATP-grasp/PIPK comment correctly, and rejects transfer of substrate, recognition surfaces, regulation, inhibitor sensitivity, and cellular role. Evidence list covers release-matched lineage, close sequence relationship, residue-level alignment, ligand-bound structures with quality checks, and biochemistry.
